text: Shock1/SBP < 80

detail.problem: Both parts present and or-ed: Shock (27942005, disorder) as a checked finding, and SBP < 80 mmHg as a routine-vital comparison with the right direction and unit. Note the footnote that defines when "shock likely" (element p73-61f8d432) is not turned into a probable Shock rule; see that element.

But the superscript 1 attaches the footnote's definition of shock to this item, and the house standard asks for a probable rule + (active_condition Shock) when the red box names a likely diagnosis; neither exists on this page.

text: Pallor with pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate ≥ 30, dizziness/weakness or chest pain

detail.problem: Logic is right: (and Pallor (or pulse>=100 RR>=30 Dizziness Asthenia Chest pain)) matches the page's "Pallor with ... or ..." reading, and all six parts are present with correct thresholds, directions and the only available rate unit (bpm). Two concept problems. (1) Pulse >= 100 is measured on "Pulse, function" (8499008), whose parent is "Cardiovascular function": it names a physiological function, not a rate. The measurable observable is "Heart rate" (364075005, parent "Cardiovascular measure"). If the routine pulse vital is recorded under Heart rate this comparison never matches, and the pulse part of the criterion is silently lost. (2) Pallor is encoded as "Pallor of skin of face" (1209208002), which narrows the page's generic "pallor" (in APC usually conjunctival/palmar pallor) to the face; "Pale discoloration of entire skin of body" is the other candidate and SNOMED has no plain "Pallor" finding, so this is a lesser concern but should be noted. "Asthenia" for weakness and the routine "Respiratory rate" concept are acceptable.
Structure matches (pallor AND any of pulse>=100, RR>=30, dizziness, weakness, chest pain). Minor: facial-only pallor concept; respiratory rate unit bpm may be a unit mismatch (breaths/min).

Structure is right: pallor AND (pulse >= 100 OR RR >= 30 OR dizziness OR weakness OR chest pain); thresholds, units and >= direction match the box (box says RR >= 30, footnote says > 30; the box value was used, correctly). Weakness -> Asthenia is acceptable. The concept is the problem: 'Pallor' is encoded as 'Pallor of skin of face' (finding), which is narrower than the page's general pallor (often judged at conjunctiva/palms). Sibling concepts such as 'Pale complexion' or 'Pale discoloration of entire skin of body' (which SNOMED returns for a 'Pallor' search) are not descendants, so a pallor recorded that way will not trigger the rule.

The grammar has no g/dL unit, so if a measurement cannot be expressed, the gap must at least be recorded and approximated (e.g. (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin below reference range" "finding")) with a Severe qualifier), not silently dropped. Pallor should be the unqualified concept (see c007).

text: Urgent level and (and complaint (or …)) structure match the box heading; the 'Pallor with …' and/or nesting is faithful. But 'Hb < 6' is missing from the or-list, so a patient with vaginal bleeding and Hb < 6 is never flagged urgent. Also, footnote 1 ('If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely') is an 'X likely' with no probable Shock diagnosis rule, so the Shock branch only fires if shock is recorded by hand.

The page's non-urgent diagnostic logic is not encoded: 'If Hb < 12, treat for likely anaemia' (stated twice, heavy periods and spotting) should be a probable (snomed_concept "Anemia" "disorder") rule with vaginal bleeding + low Hb; 'shock likely' (footnote 1) should be a probable (snomed_concept "Shock" "disorder") rule. The page's 2-week referral triggers (new bleeding > 1 year after final period, i.e. (snomed_concept "Postmenopausal bleeding" "finding"); pelvic pain; bleeding persisting after treatment) and 'bleeding from elsewhere … refer to doctor next day' are not represented in any form.
